inspiration: Terrain blended by mask: each terrain tile is a small greyscale mask (128 by 128) that decides how ground layers mix. Recreate with a few original ground textures plus our own painted or noise masks per tile, which gives many biome edges from few textures.

Meshes as readable text: the exporter rebuilds vertices and triangles from a script that Blender can run. The same idea works for us: keep a human-readable mesh form (for example glTF JSON) so diffs and reviews are possible.
Texture row order: the README notes the stored image is upside down, bottom row first. Worth a check on any import step so our textures and UVs do not come in flipped.

Hidden keepsakes: the README describes messages and photographs inside the data that never showed in normal play. Idea: a few optional notes or photos placed off the main route in our zones, with all text and art written by us.

Bundled archives: a small number of large archives, each with a directory header and then data, hold well over 100,000 resources. Idea: group our assets into a few bundles with an index so load and streaming stay simple.

briefs.label: Mask-blended ground (originals only)
briefs.why: one neutral mask per tile turns a few ground textures into many biome edges
briefs.keep: greyscale mask per tile driving two or more layered textures; masks as separate art
briefs.change: larger tile size; our own mask shapes (painted or noise); a palette per zone

briefs.label: Readable mesh pack
briefs.why: text-form meshes are easy to diff, review and repair by hand
briefs.keep: explicit vertex list and triangle list in an editable file
briefs.change: use glTF rather than a Blender script; add our own naming and LOD fields

briefs.label: Hidden keepsake
briefs.why: a small found object off the main route rewards exploration without changing the quest path
briefs.keep: optional item with a short note or photo, placed away from the route
briefs.change: our own text and art; different item shapes; placed by zone designers
